one_liner: Run an Air Force base's sexual assault prevention and response program: track cases, train responders and personnel, coordinate victim support, and advise the Wing Commander.
fit_summary: The posting needs a behavioral or social science education basis, which his M.A. in Global Affairs may meet, plus a year of GS-9-level experience in victim advocacy, social services, or sexual assault prevention and response. His resume has none of that specialized experience, and his emergency management and public health work doesn't substitute.
eligibility: Open to the public (hiring path: public); U.S. citizenship expected, with no federal status required.

Basic requirement: a behavioral or social science degree (or related field), an equivalent education/experience combination, or four years of experience showing equivalent knowledge; transcripts required if education is used.

GS-11: one year of specialized experience at GS-09 level in victim advocacy, social services, or sexual assault prevention/response; GS-12: one year at GS-11 level overseeing interpersonal-violence prevention/response programs.
Must be able to obtain and maintain a Secret clearance.
On-site at multiple Air Force installations with no telework; confirm which locations are near Manassas (e.g., Joint Base Andrews).
keywords: law enforcement and criminal investigative units
develop plans, programs, guidelines, and budgets
strategy: His resume shows no victim-advocacy, crisis-line or social-services work. Apply only if he has such experience, paid or volunteer, that isn't on the resume yet; the posting credits volunteer hours when they are listed.
Upload his George Mason transcript: an M.A. in Global Affairs should count toward the 'behavioral or social science or related' requirement, but compare the coursework with the posting's list.

Frame your IEM work around program coordination, training delivery, stakeholder and interagency coordination, and support for affected populations, using your actual title and duties; avoid claiming victim-advocacy expertise you don't have.
Answer the questionnaire conservatively: every 'expert' rating must be backed by a resume bullet, or you'll be rated not qualified.
Keep the resume to two pages, with month/year dates and hours per week for each role, and mirror the KSA wording; the posting closes 2026-12-18 but may pull applicant lists early, so apply soon.

Use this as a learning target: a role such as SAPR victim advocate (GS-09) or volunteer advocacy work with a local Northern Virginia crisis center could build qualifying experience; meanwhile, prioritize emergency-management or legislative roles that fit you better.
resume_bullets: Facilitated full-scale and tabletop exercises for federal, state and private-sector clients (2022–2024).
Took part in public health seminars on response and recovery roles (2022–2024).
interview_questions: Describe how you would respond in the first hours after being notified of a sexual assault report, including restricted versus unrestricted reporting.
How would you build working relationships with OSI, Security Forces, legal, and medical to ensure 24-hour victim advocate notification?
Tell me about a time you trained a skeptical audience on a sensitive topic.
How would you advise a Wing Commander whose prevention program metrics are declining?
watch_outs: The specialized experience requirement (victim advocacy/SAPR) is the main barrier, and consulting experience alone likely won't meet it.
A Secret clearance is required, and the role involves on-call or crisis duties typical of SAPR work.
It is on-site only, at multiple locations, so check the duty station before accepting.
Transcripts must accompany the application if education is used, and the questionnaire must match the resume exactly.
